title: Name the sounds in a room
description: List the sounds in a room and mark one you cannot identify.
oneStarDescription: Sit still and list the sounds you hear.
twoStarDescription: Point to the source of one sound, such as a vent or a clock.
threeStarDescription: Mark one sound you will not name, because you cannot find the source.

title: Name an instrument you can hear
description: Name one instrument in a recording, and say if a second sound is unknown.
oneStarDescription: Point to one sound and name the instrument if you know it.
twoStarDescription: Check the liner note, the credit, or a second listen, and correct the name if needed.
threeStarDescription: Leave a second sound unnamed if you cannot tell, and say so.

title: Note a track without guessing the animal
description: Record a track you see and leave it unnamed if you are not sure.
oneStarDescription: Describe the shape, the size relative to your hand, and where you found it.
twoStarDescription: Look for another print and say whether the direction is clear.
threeStarDescription: If you are not sure of the animal, write unknown, and do not pick a likely species.

title: Note one choice in a performance
description: Watch or listen to a live performance and name one choice the performers made.
oneStarDescription: Watch or listen to one section without checking a phone, and name what happened.
twoStarDescription: Name one choice, such as a pause, a repeat, or where someone stood.
threeStarDescription: Say what that choice did for you, and mark it as your response.

title: Note the exit when you arrive
description: When you arrive in a public room, look for the exit sign and the path, without a drill.
oneStarDescription: Find the exit sign from your seat or the door.
twoStarDescription: See whether the path from you to that sign is open.
threeStarDescription: If you are with people who asked, tell them which way the sign points.

title: Notice a label you cannot read
description: When a label is in a language you do not read, say so and find another way to the fact you need.
oneStarDescription: Say which label you cannot read.
twoStarDescription: Use a symbol, a number, or a picture on the same object.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone who reads it, or stop rather than guess the warning.

title: Notice a plant growing in a hard place
description: Notice a plant growing in a crack or a gutter and describe its spot.
oneStarDescription: Find a plant growing in a crack, a wall, or another hard spot.
twoStarDescription: Say what the spot is made of and whether the plant has light and water you can see.
threeStarDescription: Leave the plant where it is, and say why you are not pulling it.

title: Notice a repeated motif
description: Find a shape, color, or phrase that repeats in a place or a work, and say where it returns.
oneStarDescription: Point to a motif and to the second place it appears.
twoStarDescription: Say what is the same and what changes the second time.
threeStarDescription: Say what job the repeat might be doing, and mark that sentence as your guess.

title: Notice when people talk over each other
description: In a conversation you are part of, notice an overlap and make room.
oneStarDescription: Notice when two people speak at once, including yourself.
twoStarDescription: If you were one of them, stop and let the other person finish.
threeStarDescription: Ask the person who was cut off to finish, if they want to.

title: Notice word order
description: In a sentence you did not write, point to the word order that carries the meaning.
oneStarDescription: Point to who or what did the action, and the action, in someone else's sentence.
twoStarDescription: Say how the sentence would change if one phrase moved, without claiming a grammar certificate.
threeStarDescription: Find a second sentence with a different order and say what the difference does.

title: Offer a seated version of a task
description: Show how a standing task can be done from a chair, or say that it cannot.
oneStarDescription: Do one ordinary task from a chair, such as folding, reading, or sorting, and note what you cannot reach.
twoStarDescription: Bring the materials into reach, or say which part still needs standing.
threeStarDescription: Offer the seated version and the standing version, and use the one the person chooses.

title: Offer a written version of what you said
description: After you explain something aloud, offer the same points in writing.
oneStarDescription: Explain a small thing aloud.
twoStarDescription: Write the same points, not a new essay.
threeStarDescription: Ask whether the speech, the writing, or both was useful, and do not be hurt by the answer.

title: Offer guidance beside you
description: Offer your arm as a guide, describe the next change, and stop when the person lets go.
oneStarDescription: Offer your arm and wait until they take it or decline.
twoStarDescription: Before a turn, a curb, or a door, say what is coming.
threeStarDescription: If they let go or say stop, stop guiding and ask what they want next.

title: Offer water before a long task
description: Offer water before a long task and accept no.
oneStarDescription: Offer water and say where it is.
twoStarDescription: If they decline, do not insist.
threeStarDescription: If the task runs long, offer once more or point to the water, and stop there.

title: Order steps on a card
description: Put steps on a card in the order a person must do them.
oneStarDescription: Write the steps of a safe everyday task you know.
twoStarDescription: Number them so a later step does not require an earlier one you have not listed.
threeStarDescription: Have someone point to a missing step, and add it or say it belongs elsewhere.

title: Pack a shared bag from an agreed list
description: Pack a bag from a list two people agreed, and show the item you left out.
oneStarDescription: Agree a short list with the other person.
twoStarDescription: Pack those items and no surprise extra they did not ask for.
threeStarDescription: Show one thing you did not pack and why.

title: Park a topic
description: Set aside an off-topic point without losing it.
oneStarDescription: Write the off-topic point in a parking place the group can see.
twoStarDescription: Go back to the question you were on.
threeStarDescription: At the end, either schedule the parked point or say it will not be taken up, and mark which.

title: Pass an object so it can be taken
description: Pass an object handle-first, or say how the other person should take it.
oneStarDescription: Hold a tool or a cup so the other person can take the safe part.
twoStarDescription: Do not let go until they have it, or until they refuse.
threeStarDescription: If the object is hot, wet, or sharp, say so before you pass it.

title: Pick up paper with static
description: Charge a balloon or a comb and pick up a small piece of paper, then say when it stops.
oneStarDescription: Rub a balloon or a comb on dry hair or cloth and lift a bit of paper.
twoStarDescription: Touch the balloon to a wall or wait, and show that the paper no longer jumps.
threeStarDescription: Say one condition that made it weak, such as damp air, or say you could not tell.

title: Place a lamp for the work
description: Place a lamp so the work is lit and the glare is not in your eyes.
oneStarDescription: Aim a lamp at the work surface.
twoStarDescription: Move the lamp or the page until the bright spot is not in your eyes.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone whether they can see the work, and move the lamp if they cannot.

title: Plan a quiet hour for a shared space
description: Agree one quiet hour in a shared space and keep it.
oneStarDescription: Propose an hour and the space it covers.
twoStarDescription: Agree it with the other person, including one exception they need.
threeStarDescription: Keep the hour, or if you break it, say so and agree the next one.

title: Plan a visit from the opening hours
description: Use published opening hours to choose a time you can actually arrive.
oneStarDescription: Find the hours for the day you want, including a holiday note if it is there.
twoStarDescription: Choose a time inside those hours, with room to get there.
threeStarDescription: Say what you will do if you arrive and it is unexpectedly closed.

title: Point out a blocked exit
description: If you see an exit blocked, tell the person responsible and leave the fixing to them.
oneStarDescription: Point to what is blocking the exit, from a safe place.
twoStarDescription: Tell a staff member or a host what is blocking it.
threeStarDescription: Do not move a heavy or unknown object, and say why you left it.

title: Practice saying a name you find difficult
description: Ask how to say a name, practice it, and use it once.
oneStarDescription: Ask the person to say their name and listen.
twoStarDescription: Repeat it and ask if it is close enough.
threeStarDescription: Use it once in the conversation, and apologize and retry if they correct you.

title: Prepare a place for a guest to sleep
description: Prepare a sleeping place with a clear surface, a light, and a way to ask for what is missing.
oneStarDescription: Clear a surface for their bag and make the bed with clean linen if you have it.
twoStarDescription: Show the light, the toilet, and where water is.
threeStarDescription: Ask what they still need and either provide it or say you cannot.

title: Prepare one question for a guide
description: Prepare a question a guide can answer from the place, and ask it.
oneStarDescription: Write one question that is not a request for a private story.
twoStarDescription: Ask it, let the guide finish, and write the answer in their sense.
threeStarDescription: If they cannot answer, write that, and do not fill the gap yourself.

title: Print from a soft stamp
description: Cut a simple shape in a soft eraser and print it.
oneStarDescription: Draw a simple shape on an eraser and cut away what should not print.
twoStarDescription: Ink it and print it on paper so the shape is recognizable.
threeStarDescription: If the first print is muddy, clean the stamp and print a clearer one.

title: Put photographs in order
description: Put a few photographs in an order you can justify.
oneStarDescription: Look for dates, ages, or places on a small set of photos.
twoStarDescription: Put them in an order and say the clue for each step.
threeStarDescription: Leave one photo unordered if the clue is missing, and say so.

title: Read a bilingual sign
description: Read a sign in two languages and say what matches and what you cannot check.
oneStarDescription: Read both versions as far as you can.
twoStarDescription: Say one part that clearly matches, such as a place name or a time.
threeStarDescription: Mark a part you cannot verify, and do not claim the translations are equal.

title: Read a building facade
description: Describe a building from the street by its door, windows, and material.
oneStarDescription: Point to the entrance, one window pattern, and the main material.
twoStarDescription: Say which part shows you how to enter, and which is only decoration if you can tell.
threeStarDescription: Write one thing you cannot know without going inside or reading a source.

title: Read a household thermometer
description: Read a room or outdoor thermometer, including the unit, and say what you will not infer.
oneStarDescription: Say the number and whether it is Celsius or Fahrenheit.
twoStarDescription: Read it again later and say whether it rose or fell.
threeStarDescription: Say this does not tell you whether a person has a fever or whether food is safe.

title: Read a program note
description: Read a program note and say what the performance says it is, separate from your opinion.
oneStarDescription: Point to the title and one sentence about what the audience will see or hear.
twoStarDescription: Write one fact from the note and one reaction that is yours.
threeStarDescription: During or after the event, name one thing the note prepared you to notice.

title: Read a public notice
description: Read a public notice and say what it announces, who it is from, and the date.
oneStarDescription: Point to what is announced, who published it, and the date, or say which is missing.
twoStarDescription: Say who would need to act, according to the notice.
threeStarDescription: Point to the contact or the deadline, or say the notice does not give one.

title: Read how a queue works
description: Read how a queue works and take the right next step.
oneStarDescription: Read whether the queue uses a ticket, a line, or a call.
twoStarDescription: Take a ticket or join the line as the sign says.
threeStarDescription: If two signs conflict, ask a staff member instead of pushing ahead.

title: Read a size chart
description: Read a size chart and say which size matches a measurement you have.
oneStarDescription: Point to the body measurement the chart uses.
twoStarDescription: Match a measurement you took to a size, and show the row.
threeStarDescription: If you are between sizes, say so, and do not claim the garment will fit.

title: Look up a washing symbol you do not know
description: Look up one care symbol you do not know, from a chart you can show.
oneStarDescription: Copy or point to the symbol you do not know.
twoStarDescription: Find the same symbol on a care chart from the maker or a standards page you opened.
threeStarDescription: Say the action the chart gives, and do not wash the item in this skill.

title: Read an exhibition map
description: Use a gallery map to find a room and a work, then the way back.
oneStarDescription: Point to where you are on the map and to the room you want.
twoStarDescription: Go to the room and find the work number the map or list names.
threeStarDescription: Use the map to name the way back to the entrance.

title: Read steps while someone else works
description: Read instructions while another person does the task, and stop when they say stop.
oneStarDescription: Read one step, then wait until they finish it.
twoStarDescription: Repeat a step without adding advice they did not ask for.
threeStarDescription: Stop reading when they take over or when the instruction is unclear, and say which.

title: Read the care line on a tool
description: Read the one-line care note on a tool and do only that, or say you will not.
oneStarDescription: Find the maker's short care note on the tool or its card.
twoStarDescription: Do the note, such as wipe dry or store closed, and nothing more.
threeStarDescription: If there is no note and you do not know the care, do not invent a lubricant or a cleaner.

title: Read what a public question would change
description: Read a ballot or consultation question and say what it says would change, without choosing a side.
oneStarDescription: Read the question aloud as it is written.
twoStarDescription: In your own words, say what the text says would change if it passed, and point to the sentence.
threeStarDescription: Say one thing the text does not tell you, and do not add a recommendation.
